subject: Architecture
title: Elevators in Supertalls: Vertical Transit
description: A 60-second lesson on Elevators in Supertalls: Vertical Transit.

hook.text: In a 100-story tower, elevators can eat up 30% of the floor space. That's millions in lost rent.

buildup.text: Sky lobbies solve this — express elevators go to mid-levels, then local elevators spread out from there.

discovery.text: Double-deck elevators carry twice the passengers in the same shaft. The Burj uses them extensively.

twist.text: ThyssenKrupp built MULTI — a ropeless magnetic elevator that moves sideways. Shafts become networks.

climax.text: Without elevator innovation, skyscrapers above 70 floors would be economically unviable.

punchline.text: The limit of height isn't structure. It's how fast you can get people up.

quiz.question: What problem do sky lobbies solve in supertall buildings?
options: They provide emergency evacuation staging areas
They reduce the number of elevator shafts needed on lower floors
They improve cell phone reception at higher levels

details.summary: In supertall buildings, elevator design is as complex as structural engineering. Sky lobbies, double-deck cars, express zones, and destination dispatch systems solve the problem that conventional elevators would consume most of the floor area in buildings above 60 stories.
details.whyItMatters: Without intelligent elevator systems, supertall buildings would be impractical — shafts would consume all the rentable space. Elevator innovation is what makes extreme height economically viable, not just structurally possible.
takeaways: Sky lobbies reduce the number of shafts needed per floor
Double-deck cars serve two floors simultaneously
Destination dispatch groups passengers to minimize stops

faq.question: What is a sky lobby and how does it help?
faq.answer: A sky lobby is a transfer floor where passengers switch from express elevators to local ones, like changing trains at a transit hub. Express elevators bypass dozens of floors, then locals serve their zone. This reduces the total number of shafts penetrating the lower floors.

faq.question: How fast do supertall elevators travel?
faq.answer: The fastest reach over 70 km/h — Shanghai Tower's elevators hit 74 km/h. At these speeds, pressurization is needed to prevent ear discomfort. The Burj Khalifa's elevators travel at 36 km/h and cover the full height in about one minute.
